title: Adjectives
summary: Any engine can turn white and describe a noun: verbs, い-adjectives, noun + だ (the な form), and the の car.

blocks.text: You already know three kinds of engine: a **verb** (う-train), a **noun + だ** (だ-train) and an **い-adjective** (い-train). Each of them can also be turned into a **white engine**: a describing word that sits **in front of a noun** and cannot pull a train by itself. It simply tells you more about the noun behind it.
An い-adjective is already in the right shape. Put it in front of the noun.
赤いペンが小さい。 The red pen is small.

blocks.en: The red pen is small. (white engine + engine)

blocks.text: 2. Verbs: whole clauses can describe a noun
A verb in any tense can describe the noun that comes after it, and so can everything attached to it. This is not a passive; it is simply a sentence squeezed in front of a noun.

blocks.jp: 辞書を食べた犬がやんちゃだ。
blocks.en: The dog that ate the dictionary is naughty.

blocks.text: A copula engine (noun + だ) turns into **な** in front of a noun. Words that behave this way are called な-adjectives (textbooks) or adjectival nouns. They are nouns of a special class, which is why they need だ as an engine.

blocks.jp: やんちゃな犬が寝ている。

blocks.text: An ordinary noun describes another noun with **の**. It works like English 's, but it also puts something in a **class**: ピンクのドレス (a dress of the class "pink"), ウサギのオスカー (Oscar of the class "rabbit"). You do not have to memorize which nouns take の and which take な. You will pick it up from exposure, and a wrong choice is only a small mistake.

blocks.title: Four ways to describe a noun
items: **い-adjective** straight in front of the noun: **赤いペン**.
**Verb clause** in front of the noun: **歌った少女**.

questions.note: An い-adjective goes straight in front of a noun.
Noun + だ becomes な in front of a noun.
An ordinary noun describes another with の.

questions.prompt: 元気＿＿子供が走っている。
questions.note: 元気 works as a noun + だ, so it takes な.
雨 is an ordinary noun: の.

questions.instruction: Which phrase means 'the book that my younger sister read'?
questions.note: A clause goes straight in front of the noun.
便利 turns だ into な before a noun.
An い-adjective needs nothing extra.

questions.instruction: What is the noun described by the clause?
questions.note: The clause 昨日見た describes 映画.

questions.instruction: What is the job of の in 先生の本?
options: Links the owner or class to the noun
questions.note: の works like English 's.

questions.prompt: An い-adjective needs な before a noun.
questions.note: い-adjectives stay as they are: 高い山.

questions.instruction: Which word is a noun-type (な) adjective?
questions.note: きれい is a noun + だ word.
楽しい is an い-adjective.
古い describes 家 from the front.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun described by the verb clause
questions.note: 買った describes 本.
questions.en: The book (I) bought yesterday is expensive.

questions.note: の links 先生 to 車.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that uses な
questions.note: 便利な describes 店.
The white engine goes in front of its noun.

questions.prompt: The child who ate the cake is sleeping.
questions.note: A whole clause sits in front of the noun.
questions.en: The child who ate the cake is sleeping.

questions.note: の car, white engine, noun.
だ becomes な in front of the noun.

questions.prompt: In 青い空が高い the white engine is 青い.
questions.note: 青い describes 空, and 高い is the real engine.

questions.instruction: Which phrase is a verb clause describing a noun?
questions.note: 歌った is a verb in front of 少年.
